reason: The text portrays the opposite dynamic. The Israelites (the enslaved 'regular people') are depicted as oppressed victims whose liberation is sought by God through Moses and Aaron. Pharaoh (the leader of Egypt) is consistently shown as wrong—stubbornly refusing to release the people despite devastating plagues sent by God as punishment for his resistance. Even Pharaoh's own servants eventually urge him to relent, recognizing the harm his refusal is causing Egypt. The narrative clearly positions the oppressed people as wronged and their divinely-appointed leaders (Moses and Aaron) as righteous, not the other way around. Pharaoh's hardened heart and refusal to obey God's command is the central moral failing of the story.
